summary: Dirk van Hinloopen Labberton was an Indologist and linguist who earned doctorates from Leiden University and the University of Amsterdam. He taught languages at Gymnasium Willem III, Bestuursschool, and the University of Tokyo, and later served as Rector of Theosofisch Lyceum.

Divya Prakash Pathak works in computational linguistics and Indology. He earned an MA in Sanskrit from Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2023 and became a Research Scholar at the University of Delhi that same year.
Divyaraj Amiya is an Indologist and linguist. By 2026, he held positions on the faculty at the University of Tübingen and as a Temporary Teaching Fellow in Hindi at the University of Zurich.

Diwakar Acharya is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied under Albrecht Wezler at the University of Hamburg. He held faculty posts at Nepal Sanskrit University, Kyoto University, and later became a Fellow at All Souls College, Oxford.
Dixian was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Mingzu from circa 1882 to 1886. He subsequently served as abbot at Guanzong Temple from around 1912 to 1932.

Dmitrij Nikolaevič Ovsjaniko-Kulikovskij worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Saint Petersburg, Odesa, Charles, and Paris universities under Ivan Minaev and Abel Bergaigne. He held professorships at Kazan, Kharkiv, and Saint Petersburg universities.

Dmitry Aleksandrovich Suleykin was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy. From 1935 to 1938, he was a scientific researcher at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Dmitry Danilov works in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Mariupol State University, the University of Vienna, Vasyl' Stus Donetsk National University, and was a PhD candidate at the H.S. Skovoroda Institute of Philosophy in 2015.

Dmitry Kudryavsky was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev at Saint Petersburg State University and Berthold Delbrück at the University of Jena. He held posts at Saint Petersburg, the University of Tartu, and Voronezh State University.
Do Trul Tubten Changchub Gyaltsen pursued studies under both Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.

Dodrupchen Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under numerous masters, including Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö. He taught students including Ronald M. Davidson, Tulku Thondup, and Do Trul Tubten Changchub Gyaltsen.

Domenico Pezzi was an Italian linguist and Indologist who studied under Giovanni Flechia at the University of Turin, receiving his Ph.D. He subsequently spent his career at the University of Turin as an instructor and professor of Greek and comparative linguistics.

Dominic Goodall is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who completed his D.Phil. under Alexis Sanderson at Oxford. He served as Head of the École française d'Extrême-Orient in 2000 and held a post at the University of Edinburgh.

Dominic Sur is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Harvard University and the University of Virginia, completing his doctorate under David Germano. He was attested as holding a post at Utah State University in 2017.

Dominik Haas is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna under Marion Rastelli. He taught at Vienna and held research posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and the International Institute for Asian Studies.

Dominik Schröder was an ethnologist active in Tibetology, religious studies, and Iranian-Central Asian studies who completed a doctorate at Goethe University Frankfurt. He served on the Anthropos Institute and was Professor of Ethnology at Nanzan University from 1960 to 1969.

Dominik Wujastyk is an Indologist and historian of medicine who earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford. He held research and curatorial positions at the Wellcome Institute, University College London, the University of Vienna, and the University of Alberta.

Dominique Sportiche is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology between 1980 and 1984. He held an academic post at the University of California, Los Angeles starting around 1988.

Dominique Thillaud, who studied at ISC Paris and Emlyon Business School, has worked in linguistics and Indology with an affiliation at the University of Nice Sophia Antipolis (attested 1997–1998), as well as corporate positions at SNCF and Compagnie des Alpes.

Dominique-Sila Khan was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who was educated at Paris-Sorbonne University. She served as a Research Fellow at the Institute of Rajasthan Studies, attested in 2000.
